rounds.text: Jay Ambe Supermarkets Ltd is trading at a modest P/E of 21.7x [E1] while delivering exceptional financial performance that vastly outpaces its sector peers. Compounded sales growth reached 30% over three years and accelerated to 51% over the trailing twelve months, crushing the sector median sales growth of 11.9% [E8, E9, E45]. Even more impressively, compounded profit growth hit 141% over three years and 77% over the trailing twelve months, leaving the sector median profit growth of 17.4% far behind [E10, E11, E44]. This stellar top and bottom-line expansion is backed by high capital efficiency, demonstrated by a robust ROCE of 24.5% and a ROE of 20.3%, comfortably towering over the sector median ROCE of 8.7% [E6, E7, E46]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded dramatically by 11 percentage points over three years to reach 14% by March 2026, supported by a multi-year increasing margin trend and a supportive consumer services sector tailwind [E15, E16, E42]. Valuation offers a compelling entry point as a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 224 per share against the current market price of Rs 119, providing a substantial 47.0% margin of safety [E29, E30]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -14.73 Cr in March 2026, working capital days have increased from 64.6 to 100 days, and domestic institutional holdings have decreased [E20, E27, E35].

Despite headline growth figures, severe cash flow generation issues and deteriorating working capital dynamics undermine the reported profitability of Jay Ambe Supermarkets Ltd [E20, E35]. Free cash flow plunged deeply into negative territory at Rs -14.73 Cr in Mar 2026, and operating cash conversion remains weak with operating cash flow representing only 27% of operating profit [E20, E21]. Compounding these cash strains, working capital requirements have worsened significantly as working capital days stretched from 64.6 days to 100 days [E35]. Institutional confidence is heading in the wrong direction, evidenced by a negative money flow signal driven by domestic institutions slashing their holdings by 4.02 percentage points down to 7.57% [E27, E28]. Furthermore, quarterly operating margins remain inconsistent over the last three quarters and borrowings ticked upward to Rs 10.23 Cr alongside a total absence of dividend payouts [E4, E17, E23]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong multi-year compounded sales and profit growth alongside high returns on capital employed [E6, E8, E10].

Conceded: free cash flow is negative at Rs -14.73 Cr and operating cash flow represents 27% of operating profit [E20, E21], and working capital days have increased to 100 days [E35]. However, the business more than compensates with elite capital efficiency, delivering an ROCE of 24.5% and an ROE of 20.3% that massively outpace the sector medians of 8.7% and roughly 17.4% profit growth [E6, E7, E44, E46]. Domestic institutional selling [E27, E28] is handily offset by foreign institutions increasing their stake by 1.31 percentage points to 6.41% [E26], proving smart-money backing. While quarterly margins are inconsistent [E17], the yearly operating margin has expanded by 11 percentage points to 14% [E15], sitting on a multi-year uptrend [E16]. Borrowings of Rs 10.23 Cr [E23] remain tiny against a market capitalisation of Rs 105 Cr [E3], leaving debt to equity at a conservative 0.30x [E22]. Finally, the market price of Rs 119 sits 47% below a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 224 [E29, E30], and the reverse DCF indicates that today's price only prices in 9.2% growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0% [E31], offering a massive margin of safety.

Conceded: ROCE of 24.5% and ROE of 20.3% significantly outpace sector medians [E6, E7, E46]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash generation metrics glosses over a severe structural disconnect where free cash flow plunges to negative Rs -14.73 Cr and operating cash flow converts at a paltry 27% of operating profit [E20, E21]. Furthermore, working capital bloat has accelerated from 64.6 to 100 days [E35], directly invalidating the sustainability of reported earnings and masking the heavy cash burn required to drive that top-line growth. While the bull cites foreign institutional accumulation of 1.31 percentage points [E26], it ignores a much larger domestic institutional exodus of 4.02 percentage points [E27], resulting in an overall negative institutional money flow of -2.71 percentage points [E28]. Although debt-to-equity is low at 0.30x [E22], absolute borrowings have actually expanded to Rs 10.23 Cr [E23], coinciding with an inconsistent quarterly margin trend [E17] and zero dividend payouts despite reported profits [E34]. Finally, the reliance on a model-driven DCF value of Rs 224 [E29] ignores the market's verdict reflected in the stock languishing at just 28% of its 52-week range [E5].
